cashTip: Carry small dirham notes for meals, taxis and markets; cards work mainly in hotels and bigger restaurants.
name: Chefchaouen
tagline: The blue-washed town in the Rif mountains
summary: Chefchaouen's medina is painted in every shade of blue, climbing a mountainside in the Rif. It's a relaxed place to wander lanes, sip mint tea in the kasbah square, watch sunset from the Spanish Mosque and hike to waterfalls nearby.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are best. Summer is warm and busy with domestic visitors. Winters are cold and wet.
arrival: Buses from Fez take about 4 hours and from Tangier about 3. Grand taxis are faster.
gettingAround: Walk the medina; taxis to Akchour.
foodTip: Local goat cheese, bissara soup and tagines.
buyTip: Woven blankets, wool and blue pigments.

connections.note: CTM buses; grand taxis are quicker.

items.name: Blue medina lanes
items.summary: Lanes, stairs and doorways washed in blue, with potted plants and cats.
items.expect: Respect residents' doors and privacy when photographing.
items.tip: Go early morning for empty lanes.

items.name: Kasbah and Outa el-Hammam square
items.summary: A red-walled kasbah with a garden and small museum beside the main square.

items.name: Spanish Mosque viewpoint
items.summary: A ruined mosque on a hill above town, the classic sunset viewpoint.
items.why: The best view of the blue town.

items.name: Ras el-Maa spring
items.summary: A spring and stream where locals wash and cafés sit by the water.
items.tip: Stop on the way up to the mosque.

items.name: Akchour waterfalls
items.summary: Hikes along a river canyon to waterfalls and the God's Bridge rock arch.
items.tip: Wear shoes that can get wet.

items.name: Talassemtane National Park
items.summary: Cedar and fir forests with village-to-village trekking.

items.name: Goat cheese
items.summary: Fresh local goat cheese served with olive oil and bread.
items.expect: Sold by village women in the market.

items.name: Bissara
items.summary: A warm fava-bean soup with olive oil and cumin.

items.name: Tagine with a view
items.summary: Slow-cooked tagines of lamb, chicken or vegetables on rooftop terraces.

cashTip: Carry small dirham notes for meals, taxis and markets; cards work mainly in hotels and bigger restaurants.
name: Essaouira
tagline: A breezy Atlantic port of ramparts, gulls and kitesurfers
summary: Essaouira is a laid-back fortified port on the Atlantic, with a white-and-blue medina, sea ramparts used in Game of Thrones, a busy fishing harbour and a wide windy beach for kitesurfing. It's a calm contrast to Marrakech, three hours away.
seasonNote: Mild year-round; summer is cooler than inland but very windy, perfect for kitesurfing. The Gnaoua music festival is in June.
arrival: Buses from Marrakech take about 3 hours. A small airport has a few European flights.
foodTip: Grilled sardines and fish at the port, tagines and amlou almond-argan spread.
buyTip: Thuya wood boxes, argan oil and paintings.

items.name: Skala de la Ville ramparts
items.summary: Sea walls lined with old bronze cannons, crashing waves below.

items.name: Fishing port
items.summary: Blue boats, gulls and fish auctions, with a fortress tower to climb.
items.tip: Go in the morning when boats return.

items.name: Medina
items.summary: A UNESCO-listed walled town of white houses and craft workshops.

items.name: Beach and kitesurfing
items.summary: A long sandy bay with strong trade winds for kite and windsurfing.
items.expect: Too windy for sunbathing at times.

items.name: Argan oil cooperative
items.summary: Women's cooperatives cracking and pressing argan nuts.
items.expect: Watch for goats in argan trees on the road.

items.name: Diabat and the dunes
items.summary: A village linked to Jimi Hendrix legend, with dunes and a ruined fort.
items.expect: Walk or ride along the beach.
items.tip: Ride a horse or camel down the beach.

items.name: Port fish grills
items.summary: Pick fish at the stalls and they grill it for you.

items.name: Fish tagine
items.summary: Fish tagine with tomato, peppers and preserved lemon.

items.name: Amlou
items.summary: Almond, argan oil and honey spread with bread.

cashTip: Carry small dirham notes for meals, taxis and markets; cards work mainly in hotels and bigger restaurants.
name: Merzouga
tagline: Sahara dunes, camel treks and desert stars
summary: Merzouga is a village at the edge of Erg Chebbi, a sea of orange dunes rising up to 150 m. Ride a camel into the dunes at sunset, sleep in a desert camp under the stars and wake for sunrise over the Sahara.
seasonNote: October to April is best. December nights are freezing. Summer is extremely hot and can bring sandstorms.
arrival: It's about 9 hours by road from Marrakech or 7 from Fez; most visitors come on a 3-day tour. Overnight Supratours buses run from Fez and Marrakech.
foodTip: Madfouna 'Berber pizza', tagines and mint tea.
buyTip: Fossils from the region and Berber rugs.
baseArea: A desert camp in the dunes, or a kasbah hotel at the edge

connections.note: Usually a 3-day tour via Ait Benhaddou and Todra Gorge.

items.name: Erg Chebbi camel trek
items.summary: A camel ride into the dunes at sunset, with views from a high ridge.
items.tip: Climb a dune on foot for sunset.

items.name: Desert camp night
items.summary: A night in a Berber tent camp with drumming and a sky full of stars.
items.expect: Camps vary from basic to luxury.
items.tip: Step away from camp lights to stargaze.

items.name: Sandboarding
items.summary: Board down the steep faces of the dunes.
items.tip: Climb high for a long run.

items.name: Khamlia Gnawa village
items.summary: A village of Gnawa musicians whose ancestors came from West Africa.
items.expect: Music and tea for a donation.

items.name: Rissani market
items.summary: A traditional market town with a 'donkey parking' and spice stalls.
items.expect: Main market days are Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday.

items.name: Todra Gorge
items.summary: Sheer 300 m canyon walls closing in on a river.

items.name: Madfouna
items.summary: A 'Berber pizza' of bread stuffed with meat and spices, baked in sand.

items.name: Camp tagine
items.summary: Tagine cooked over charcoal at camp.

items.name: Mint tea
items.summary: Sweet green tea with mint, poured from a height.

cashTip: Carry small dirham notes for meals, taxis and markets; cards work mainly in hotels and bigger restaurants.
name: Casablanca
tagline: Morocco's modern city and a mosque over the sea
summary: Casablanca is Morocco's biggest city and business capital. Its highlight is the vast Hassan II Mosque on the Atlantic, one of the few in Morocco open to non-Muslims, along with Art Deco boulevards, the Habous quarter and a seaside corniche.
seasonNote: Mild all year. Summer is warm and humid; winter is cool and rainy.
arrival: Mohammed V Airport is 45 minutes by train. Al Boraq high-speed trains link Tangier in about 2 hours; trains to Marrakech take about 2.5.
foodTip: Seafood from the central market, msemen pancakes and Friday couscous.
buyTip: Crafts and spices in the Habous quarter.
baseArea: City centre or near the corniche

items.name: Hassan II Mosque
items.summary: A huge mosque on the ocean with a 210 m minaret and a hall for 25,000.
items.expect: Guided tours for non-Muslims outside prayer times.
items.why: One of the world's largest mosques.

items.name: Ain Diab corniche
items.summary: A seafront promenade of beach clubs and cafés.

items.name: Habous quarter
items.summary: A 1930s 'new medina' of arches, bookshops and pastry shops.

items.name: Art Deco centre
items.summary: Boulevards of French-era Art Deco and Mauresque buildings.

items.name: Rick's Café
items.summary: A restaurant recreating the bar from the film Casablanca, with a piano.
items.tip: Ask the pianist for 'As Time Goes By'.

items.name: Museum of Moroccan Judaism
items.summary: The Arab world's only Jewish museum, on Morocco's Jewish heritage.
items.tip: Ask staff about the community's history.

items.name: Rabat
items.summary: Morocco's capital, with the Kasbah of the Udayas, Hassan Tower and royal mausoleum.

items.name: Central market seafood
items.summary: Pick fresh fish and oysters at the market and have them cooked nearby.

items.name: Msemen
items.summary: Flaky square pancakes with honey or cheese.

items.name: Friday couscous
items.summary: Couscous with seven vegetables, traditionally eaten on Fridays.
items.expect: Many cafés serve it only on Friday.

cashTip: Keep small Egyptian pound notes for tips, taxis and markets; major sites take cards. Agree prices before rides.
name: Aswan
tagline: Feluccas, Nubian villages and the road to Abu Simbel
summary: Aswan is Egypt's most relaxed city, where the Nile flows between granite islands and golden dunes. Sail a felucca, visit the island temple of Philae and colourful Nubian villages, and make the pre-dawn trip to the colossal temples of Abu Simbel.
seasonNote: November to February is warm and sunny. Summer is extremely hot, often above 40°C.
arrival: Flights from Cairo take about 1.5 hours. Trains from Luxor take about 3 hours, and Nile cruises link the two.
foodTip: Nubian dishes, ful medames, koshary and karkade hibiscus tea.
buyTip: Spices, Nubian baskets and karkade from the souk.
baseArea: The Corniche or a Nubian guesthouse on the west bank

connections.note: Or a 3 to 4 night Nile cruise.

items.name: Philae Temple
items.summary: The temple of Isis, moved stone by stone to an island to save it from the dam's waters.
items.expect: Boat from the jetty; agree a price.
items.tip: Stay for the sound and light show.

items.name: Abu Simbel
items.summary: Ramesses II's four colossal statues carved into a cliff, moved to save them from Lake Nasser.
items.expect: About 3.5 hours each way; leave around 4 am.
items.tip: Go on 22 February or October for the sun festival.
items.why: One of the world's great monuments.

items.name: Felucca sail
items.summary: A sailboat around Elephantine and Kitchener's islands at sunset.

items.name: Nubian village
items.summary: Brightly painted houses in Gharb Soheil, with tea, henna and local crafts.

items.name: Unfinished Obelisk
items.summary: A giant obelisk abandoned in the quarry when it cracked.

items.name: Nubian Museum
items.summary: Nubia's history from prehistory to the villages lost to Lake Nasser.

items.name: Tombs of the Nobles
items.summary: Rock tombs of Old Kingdom governors with views over the river.

items.name: Kom Ombo Temple
items.summary: A double temple to the crocodile god Sobek and the falcon god Horus.

items.name: Nubian dinner
items.summary: Stews, bread and grilled fish in a Nubian guesthouse.

items.name: Ful medames
items.summary: Stewed fava beans with oil, cumin and bread.

items.name: Karkade
items.summary: Hibiscus tea, hot or iced, grown locally.
items.tip: Buy dried flowers to take home.

cashTip: Keep small Egyptian pound notes for tips, taxis and markets; major sites take cards. Agree prices before rides.
name: Hurghada
tagline: Red Sea reefs, desert and beach resorts
summary: Hurghada is Egypt's busiest Red Sea resort, with coral reefs offshore, island beaches, desert safaris and the lagoon town of El Gouna nearby. It's also a base for day trips to Luxor.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are warm with comfortable sea temperatures. Summer is very hot; winter evenings are cool.
arrival: Hurghada Airport has flights from Cairo and across Europe. Visas are available on arrival for many nationalities, but check current rules.
foodTip: Fresh seafood, koshary and Bedouin barbecue.
baseArea: Sahl Hasheesh, El Gouna or Hurghada Marina

items.name: Giftun Island
items.summary: Boat trips to snorkel reefs and relax on white island beaches.

items.name: Reef diving
items.summary: Dive sites full of coral, turtles and dolphins.

items.name: El Gouna
items.summary: A lagoon town of canals, beaches and kitesurf spots.

items.name: Hurghada Marina
items.summary: A waterfront of cafés, yachts and evening strolls.

items.name: Desert safari
items.summary: Quad bikes or jeeps to a Bedouin camp for tea and stars.
items.expect: Choose an operator with good reviews.

items.name: Luxor day trip
items.summary: Karnak, the Valley of the Kings and more on a long day trip.

items.name: Seafood restaurants
items.summary: Choose fish and prawns by weight, grilled or fried.

items.name: Koshary
items.summary: Rice, lentils and pasta with tomato sauce and crispy onions.

items.name: Bedouin barbecue
items.summary: Grilled meat and bread at a desert camp.
items.tip: Ask for vegetarian dishes in advance.

cashTip: Keep small Egyptian pound notes for tips, taxis and markets; major sites take cards. Agree prices before rides.
name: Alexandria
tagline: Egypt's Mediterranean city of Cleopatra and the great library
summary: Founded by Alexander the Great, Alexandria was the ancient world's centre of learning. Today it's a breezy Mediterranean city of corniche cafés, the modern Bibliotheca Alexandrina, a fort on the site of the Pharos lighthouse and Roman catacombs.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are mild. Summer is crowded with Egyptian holidaymakers. Winter is cool, rainy and stormy.
arrival: Trains from Cairo take about 2.5 hours. Borg El Arab Airport is about an hour away.
gettingAround: Old trams, taxis and Careem along the corniche.
foodTip: Fresh fish by weight, Alexandrian liver sandwiches and feteer.
buyTip: Antiques and old books near Attarin.
baseArea: Along the corniche near Raml Station

items.name: Bibliotheca Alexandrina
items.summary: A striking modern library honouring the ancient one, with museums inside.

items.name: Citadel of Qaitbay
items.summary: A 15th-century fort on the site of the ancient Pharos lighthouse.

items.name: Catacombs of Kom el-Shoqafa
items.summary: Roman-era tombs mixing Egyptian, Greek and Roman art.

items.name: Pompey's Pillar
items.summary: A 27 m Roman granite column on the site of the Serapeum.

items.name: Corniche
items.summary: A long seafront road with cafés and old hotels.
items.tip: Have coffee at a historic café.

items.name: Montaza Palace gardens
items.summary: Royal gardens and beaches around a 1930s palace.

items.name: Roman Amphitheatre
items.summary: Egypt's only Roman amphitheatre, with baths and villas with mosaics.
items.tip: See the Villa of the Birds mosaics.

items.name: El Alamein
items.summary: WWII cemeteries and a military museum on the desert battlefield.

items.name: Fish restaurants
items.summary: Pick fish and shrimp by weight, grilled or baked in clay.

items.name: Alexandrian liver sandwich
items.summary: Spicy fried liver with peppers in bread.

items.name: Feteer
items.summary: Flaky layered pastry, sweet or savoury.
items.tip: Try it with honey and cream.
